mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising risk-free rates and discounting future corporate cash flows, which reduces S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a contraction in real economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE and a fall in PAYEMS signals labor market imbalances (tightness with stagnant employment growth), which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month + 0.3% AND PAYEMS < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -1% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS signals weakening housing demand despite elevated inventory, which reduces construction and home-related spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 2% AND RSAFS < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly CPIAUCSL above 3% for four consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts aggressive central bank tightening and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in GDPC1 below -1% for two consecutive quarters signals broad-based demand weakness, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
